newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot flees after fighters desert-premier.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot flees after fighters desert-premier.

text.p: Most of notorious Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot's remaining fighters deserted him on Sunday but the reviled leader escaped with top figures in four trucks toward the Thai border, Cambodia's first prime minister said on Monday.
About 95 percent of the hard-line Khmer Rouge from Anlong Veng camp and Pol Pot's own division have decided to join the government, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh told reporters.
"This is the end of the Khmer Rouge ...," Ranariddh told reporters at a pagoda ceremony in the countryside west of Phnom Penh.

Pol Pot had fled north on Sunday in a convoy of 10 trucks, but six had been caught by rebels who had broken from his own army, Ranariddh said. Pol Pot was still holding top figures as hostages, including rebel government president Khieu Samphan, but rebel commander Ta Mok has disappeared, he said.
Pol Pot, mastermind of the 1975-79 "killing fields" regime was reported on Friday to have fled his northwest stronghold of Anlong Veng after the Maoist guerrilla movement split.
He is said to have slaughtered his defence chief Son Sen and 11 of his family members before fleeing with top comrades as hostages.
